system:
You are working out the chronology of a compulsory third party motor accident claim in New South Wales, from a list of things recorded about decided claims.

Divide the life of a claim into ordered PHASES, and place every recorded item in the phase at which the thing it measures COMES INTO EXISTENCE -- not when it is written down, and not when it is used.

Each item is labelled with WHAT IT IS A PROPERTY OF. Use that as the decisive test: an item arises when the entity it is a property of arises. A property of the collision arises at the collision, however long afterwards it is written down. A property of a relationship between two things cannot arise until both of those things exist. A property of the proceeding arises when the proceeding is under way.

That distinction decides most of the hard cases:
  * A medical assessment performed years later measures a physical state that arose at the time of the injury. Ask when the QUANTITY was fixed, not when it was measured.
  * Something recorded in the final decision may describe a fact established long before it.
  * A procedural fact about how the claim was run belongs to the phase in which the claim was run, not to the injury.

Decide how many phases there are. Use as few as genuinely capture the order and no more; a phase containing one item is fine if that item really stands alone in time. Items that arise at the same stage belong in the same phase, and a phase may contain items that cause one another -- being contemporaneous is not being simultaneous.

For every item, say in one sentence WHEN the thing it measures came into existence. That sentence is the justification for its placement and will be recorded.
user:
Recorded about each decided claim:
  - Lump Sum: the total dollars awarded. The final figure the decision arrives at, made up of the heads of damage plus components the table does not itemise
  - WPI %: whole person impairment as a percentage. A CLINICAL assessment of the permanent impairment remaining once the condition has stabilised after treatment -- not a measure of injury severity at the moment of impact
  - Non-Economic Loss: dollars awarded for pain and suffering. A component of the award, quantified in the decision
  - Future Economic Loss: dollars awarded for loss of future earning capacity. A component of the award, computed from pre-accident earnings, residual working capacity and the years remaining to retirement
  - Claimant Weekly Income: what the claimant was earning per week BEFORE the collision. A fact about their working life prior to the accident
  - Claimant Age: the claimant's age at the date of injury. Fixed at birth and unaffected by anything in the claim
  - Claimant Gender: the claimant's recorded gender. Unaffected by anything in the claim
  - Nature: which procedural route the claim took: approval of an agreed settlement, or a contested damages assessment. A fact about how the proceeding resolved
  - Injury Burden Intensity: the overall PHYSICAL severity of the injuries the claimant sustained. The physical counterpart of Psychological Injury Emphasis; both measure harm inflicted by the collision itself
  - Treatment Burden: the extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care the claimant underwent. This care is delivered over the months and years FOLLOWING the injury
  - Work Impact Severity: how much working capacity the claimant lost. Incapacity emerges as the injury and its treatment run their course after the accident
  - Legal Procedural Complexity: how procedurally heavy the proceeding was -- interlocutory steps, volume of evidence, hearings. A property of how the claim was litigated. It is driven by what ends up contested: disputed fault, disputed causation, and a prior condition to apportion against all generate argument and evidence
  - Psychological Injury Emphasis: the SEVERITY of the psychological injury the claimant suffered as a result of the accident. This is the psychological counterpart of Injury Burden Intensity and is the same kind of quantity: a measure of harm inflicted by the collision. The column name is misleading -- the score is read off how the decision discusses the injury, but what it measures is the injury
  - Liability Clarity: how clear it is WHO WAS AT FAULT in the collision. Fault is fixed by the circumstances of the accident itself; the claim later establishes it but does not change it. Whether liability is contested is what drives argument later on
  - Causation Complexity: how hard it is to attribute the claimant's condition to the accident rather than to something else. It is the downstream result of weighing the accident's injuries -- physical and psychological -- against any pre-existing condition, and so follows once those are established
  - Pre-existing Condition Salience: how prominently a condition the claimant ALREADY HAD BEFORE THE ACCIDENT features in the decision. The condition itself pre-dates the collision entirely; only its prominence in the reasons is established later

Define the ordered phases of a claim, then place every item in one.

phases.name: Claimant Existence Phase
phases.description: This phase includes details about the claimant that exist from before any collision occurred, such as their age, gender, and income.

phases.name: Collision and Injury Phase
phases.description: This phase captures all immediate results of the accident itself, including physical and psychological injuries and liability.

phases.name: Post-Collision Consequence Phase
phases.description: In this phase, the effects and aftermath of the sustained injuries take shape, such as ongoing treatment and work impact.

phases.name: Causation and Pre-existing Consideration Phase
phases.description: During this phase, the complexities of attributing the effects to the accident as opposed to other causes, including pre-existing conditions, are evaluated.

phases.name: Proceeding Conduct Phase
phases.description: In this phase, procedural choices and the complexity of the legal proceeding arise from the handling of the case.

phases.name: Final Determination Phase
phases.description: This phase covers the final decisions made regarding the claim, such as settlement amounts and total liability.

assignments.when_it_arises: The Lump Sum is determined in the final decision when the claim is resolved.
The WPI % arises once the injury has stabilized and permanent impairment can be assessed after treatment.
The Non-Economic Loss is quantified at the end of the claim as part of the damages awarded.
The Future Economic Loss is determined in the final decision as part of the overall award.
Claimant Weekly Income exists as a fact about the claimant's earnings prior to the collision.
The claimant's age is fixed at birth and exists before the claim is made.
Claimant Gender is a fact about the claimant that existed before any collision.
The Nature of the claim is determined by how it resolves, either by settlement or contested assessment.
Injury Burden Intensity is determined by the severity of injuries sustained during the collision.
Treatment Burden unfolds as the claimant undergoes medical care over time after the collision.
Work Impact Severity manifests as the extent of incapacity is realized following the injury and treatment.
Legal Procedural Complexity comes into being as the procedural aspects of the legal proceeding unfold.
Psychological Injury Emphasis emerges as a measure of psychological harm inflicted by the collision.
Liability Clarity is fixed by the circumstances of the collision at the time it occurs.
Causation Complexity arises as the relationship between the accident and the claimant's condition is analyzed.
Pre-existing Condition Salience arises as how prominently existing conditions factor into the decision is determined.
